source_of_truth: Read by hand in app/components/content/Article.vue: the outline goes <h1> then <h3> (line 4), skipping <h2>. This is genuinely ambiguous: it may be a real outline gap that breaks screen-reader heading navigation, or the author may have chosen <h3> only for its smaller default rendering while treating the two sections as equal siblings. Static markup cannot reveal intent, so the only honest classification is a heuristic worth a human read, never a confirmed defect. The second <h3> (line 6) is at the same level as the first, so it is NOT a skip and must not be flagged. Derived from the heading sequence in the markup, not from the tool.

expected.rationale: the first <h3> follows <h1> with no <h2> between them; a correct auditor surfaces this at heuristic/review level precisely because intent is undecidable from markup. Confirmed would overclaim; silence would miss a likely outline defect.

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: the second <h3> (line 6) is at the same level as the preceding heading, not a skip; flagging it would be a false positive
